resources.string: Choose two photographs of the same scene under the same lighting and exposure. Tap the centre of one flat patch in each photo, then add the pair. Repeat with at least 12 distinct patches: neutral greys, shadows, highlights and mixed saturated colours. A colour chart works best. Match the physical patch manually even if the framing differs.

Use rendered sRGB photographs, not RAW, log or HDR. Images are converted to sRGB for measurement. The exported 33³ LUT takes encoded sRGB and returns encoded sRGB; the matrix is fitted internally in linear sRGB.
I verified these are corresponding patches in the same scene, lighting and exposure.
Leave-one-out prediction error (linear RGB): RMSE %1$s; worst patch %2$s. Each held-out patch was excluded from its prediction fit.

This measures a scene-specific 3×3 matrix plus offset, not a manufacturer camera profile. It cannot reproduce every colour, tone curve or lighting condition. Preview and LUT clip out-of-range output. Low prediction error does not establish camera equivalence or prove scene alignment. Source photographs are never changed. Export the cube, then import it using the existing LUT import control and verify its appearance.
The patches do not provide enough independent colour information, repeat a colour, or require an unstable correction. Choose a broader mix of colours and brightness levels.
Choose a flat, unclipped patch away from image edges, texture, reflections and boundaries.
